description: An introduction to magnets, magnetic materials, magnetic fields, methods of making and destroying magnetism, the Earth's magnetism, and everyday applications of magnets.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following materials is attracted by a magnet?
mcq.explanation: Iron is a magnetic material, so it is attracted by a magnet, while copper, wood and plastic are non-magnetic.

mcq.questionText: What name is given to the two ends of a bar magnet where the magnetism is strongest?
mcq.explanation: The ends of a magnet are called poles, and the magnetic force is strongest at the poles.

mcq.questionText: When two magnets are brought close together, what happens between a north pole and another north pole?
mcq.explanation: Like poles repel each other, so two north poles push apart.

mcq.questionText: A freely suspended bar magnet always comes to rest pointing in which direction?
mcq.explanation: Because of the Earth's magnetism, a freely suspended magnet rests in the North-South direction.

mcq.questionText: Which instrument uses a small magnetic needle to show direction?
mcq.explanation: A magnetic compass has a small magnet that aligns with the Earth's magnetic field to indicate direction.

mcq.questionText: Magnetic field lines around a bar magnet are drawn pointing from which pole to which pole outside the magnet?
mcq.explanation: By convention, magnetic field lines leave the north pole and enter the south pole outside the magnet.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a method of making a magnet?
mcq.explanation: Stroking a steel bar with a magnet is one way to make a magnet; heating, hammering and dropping tend to destroy magnetism.

mcq.questionText: In the electrical method of making a magnet, what is passed through a coil wound around the steel bar?
mcq.explanation: A direct current passed through a coil (solenoid) around the steel magnetises it.

mcq.questionText: Which process is used to remove magnetism from a magnet?
mcq.explanation: Demagnetisation is the process of destroying the magnetism of a magnet.

mcq.questionText: Which of these would NOT cause a magnet to lose its magnetism?
mcq.explanation: Storing magnets with soft-iron keepers preserves magnetism, while heat, hammering and dropping destroy it.

mcq.questionText: A material that can be magnetised but easily loses its magnetism is called a:
mcq.explanation: Soft magnetic materials such as soft iron are easy to magnetise but lose their magnetism quickly.

mcq.questionText: Where around a bar magnet are the magnetic field lines closest together?
mcq.explanation: Field lines are closest together near the poles, showing that the field is strongest there.

mcq.questionText: Which metal is commonly used to make permanent magnets because it keeps its magnetism?
mcq.explanation: Steel is a hard magnetic material that retains its magnetism, making it suitable for permanent magnets.

mcq.questionText: What is produced in the region around a magnet where its force can be felt?
mcq.explanation: The region around a magnet where its magnetic force acts is called the magnetic field.

mcq.questionText: How are magnets best stored to prevent loss of magnetism?

options.text: In bar pairs with unlike poles together and keepers across the ends

mcq.explanation: Bar magnets are stored in pairs with unlike poles next to each other and soft-iron keepers across the ends to keep the field closed.

fib.questionText: A device or material that attracts iron and certain other metals is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A magnet is an object that produces a magnetic field and attracts magnetic materials.

fib.questionText: Materials that are not attracted by a magnet are called _____ materials.
fib.explanation: Non-magnetic materials such as wood, plastic and copper are not attracted by magnets.

fib.questionText: Like poles of magnets _____ each other.
fib.explanation: Like poles repel while unlike poles attract.

fib.questionText: Unlike poles of magnets _____ each other.
fib.explanation: A north pole and a south pole attract each other.

fib.questionText: The pole of a freely suspended magnet that points towards the Earth's geographic north is called the _____ pole.
fib.explanation: The north-seeking pole points towards the geographic north of the Earth.

fib.questionText: Making a nearby piece of iron a temporary magnet just by bringing a magnet close to it is called magnetic _____.
fib.explanation: In magnetic induction, a magnetic material becomes a magnet without touching the magnet.

fib.questionText: Strongly _____ a magnet is one way to destroy its magnetism.
fib.explanation: Heating a magnet to a high temperature disturbs its arrangement and destroys magnetism.

fib.questionText: Soft pieces of iron placed across the poles of stored magnets to preserve magnetism are called _____.
fib.explanation: Keepers complete the magnetic circuit and help magnets keep their strength during storage.

fib.questionText: Iron filings sprinkled around a magnet line up to show the pattern of the magnetic _____.
fib.explanation: Iron filings reveal the shape of the magnetic field lines around a magnet.

fib.questionText: A coil of wire wound into many turns used in the electrical method of magnetising is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A solenoid carrying a direct current behaves like a magnet and can magnetise steel placed inside it.

tf.questionText: A magnet attracts both iron and plastic.
tf.explanation: A magnet attracts iron but not plastic, which is a non-magnetic material.

tf.questionText: Every magnet has two poles, a north pole and a south pole.
tf.explanation: All magnets have at least one north and one south pole; a single isolated pole cannot exist.

tf.questionText: Two north poles brought together will attract each other.
tf.explanation: Two north poles are like poles, so they repel each other.

tf.questionText: The magnetic force of a bar magnet is strongest at its centre.
tf.explanation: The magnetic force is strongest at the poles, not at the centre.

tf.questionText: A compass works because of the Earth's magnetism.
tf.explanation: The compass needle aligns with the Earth's magnetic field to show direction.

tf.questionText: Steel keeps its magnetism longer than soft iron.
tf.explanation: Steel is a hard magnetic material and retains magnetism, while soft iron loses it quickly.

tf.questionText: Stroking a steel bar repeatedly with one end of a magnet can make it a magnet.
tf.explanation: The stroking method magnetises steel by repeatedly drawing a magnet pole along it in one direction.

tf.questionText: Hammering a magnet hard will increase its magnetism.
tf.explanation: Hammering disturbs the arrangement inside the magnet and weakens or destroys its magnetism.

tf.questionText: Magnetic field lines never cross one another.
tf.explanation: Field lines never cross because the field has only one direction at any point.

tf.questionText: If a bar magnet is cut in half, each piece will have only one pole.
tf.explanation: Cutting a magnet produces two smaller magnets, each with its own north and south pole.

summary.correctAnswer: A magnet is a material that attracts iron and points north-south when free to turn.
summary.explanation: Magnets attract magnetic materials and have a direction-finding property.

summary.correctAnswer: Magnetic materials (iron, steel, nickel, cobalt) are attracted by magnets; non-magnetic ones are not.
summary.explanation: Only a few metals are magnetic; most materials are non-magnetic.

summary.correctAnswer: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.
summary.explanation: This basic law governs how magnets interact.

summary.correctAnswer: A magnet is strongest at its poles.
summary.explanation: The poles concentrate the magnetic force.

summary.correctAnswer: A magnetic field is the region around a magnet where its force acts.
summary.explanation: Field lines go from north to south outside the magnet.

summary.correctAnswer: Magnets can be made by stroking, by electric current, and by induction.
summary.explanation: These three methods all align the magnetic material to create poles.

summary.correctAnswer: Magnetism is destroyed by heating, hammering, dropping, or using alternating current.
summary.explanation: These actions disturb the orderly arrangement inside the magnet.

summary.correctAnswer: Soft iron is easily magnetised but loses it quickly; steel is harder to magnetise but keeps it.
summary.explanation: Soft materials make temporary magnets; hard materials make permanent magnets.

summary.correctAnswer: The Earth behaves like a giant magnet, which is why a compass points north-south.
summary.explanation: The Earth's magnetic field guides compass needles.

summary.correctAnswer: Store magnets in pairs with unlike poles together and keepers, and avoid heat and dropping.
summary.explanation: Proper storage keeps magnets strong for longer.

hoq.questionText: A student has two identical-looking steel bars; one is a magnet and one is not. Using only the two bars and no other equipment, how can the student tell which one is the magnet?

options.text: Bring an end of one bar to the middle of the other; the magnet attracts strongly but its own middle attracts weakly, so test which bar's middle gives no strong pull
Heat both bars and see which one bends
Drop both bars and listen for sound

hoq.explanation: A magnet has strong poles but a weak centre; touching an end of one bar to the centre of the other shows no strong attraction only when the centre of the magnet is used, identifying the magnet.

hoq.questionText: Two bar magnets are placed end to end with their unlike poles facing each other and iron filings are sprinkled around. What pattern of field lines forms in the gap between them?

options.text: No lines appear in the gap
Lines run directly across the gap from the north pole to the south pole
Lines curve away from the gap on both sides
Lines cross each other in the gap

hoq.explanation: Between unlike poles the fields combine, so field lines run straight across the gap from north to south, showing attraction.

hoq.questionText: A factory needs an electromagnet that can be switched on to lift scrap iron and switched off to release it. Which core material and method should be chosen, and why?

options.text: A steel core magnetised by stroking, because steel keeps its magnetism
A soft-iron core with a current-carrying coil, because soft iron loses its magnetism when the current stops
A copper core with a permanent magnet attached
A plastic core heated until it is magnetic

hoq.explanation: A soft-iron core in a coil becomes a strong magnet only while current flows and loses its magnetism when switched off, allowing the load to be released.
